# Stella Maynard

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>
- **Status:** poor  <sub>[v3 c10 P52](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** schoolteacher  <sub>[v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v4 c1 P22](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0022)</sub>
- **Titles:** rose-red girl  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

Stella is a vivid, black-eyed young woman noted for her good looks. During her time at Queen's Academy, she was considered to carry off the palm for beauty in the Second Year classes.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)_

## Personality

Stella is thoughtful, imaginative, and ambitious, harboring a heart full of aerial, rainbow-like wistful dreams and fancies. She values living in Patty's Place with her close friends, viewing it as a warm nest compared to boardinghouses. At times she experiences blue, discouraged moods where she questions the worth of living and feels her thoughts are unoriginal.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c27 P10](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0010), [v3 c35 P31](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0031)_

## History

Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy, where she studied in the Second Year classes and formed a close circle of intimate friends with Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant. After her time at Queen's, she spent time working as a schoolteacher. She later wrote to Anne proposing that they rent Patty's Place together so she could attend Redmond College while her aunt kept house for them. During her college years, she lived at Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, Philippa Gordon, and her Aunt Jamesina, achieving a good all-round academic standing at graduation. After completing her studies, Stella moved to Vancouver, where she resumed teaching school.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c9 P6](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0006), [v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v3 c10 P47](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0047), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c37 P29](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0029), [v4 c1 P22](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0022), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)_

## Quotes

> I’m so glad we can keep Patty’s Place for another year. I was afraid they’d come back. And then our jolly little nest here would be broken up—and we poor callow nestlings thrown out on the cruel world of boardinghouses again.  <sub>[v3 c27 P10](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0010)</sub>

> I’m blue and discouraged myself. Nothing seems worthwhile. My very thoughts are old. I’ve thought them all before. What is the use of living after all, Anne?  <sub>[v3 c35 P31](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0031)</sub>

> It does—but I am not jealous. I love Anne and I like Roy. Everybody says she is making a brilliant match, and even Mrs. Gardner thinks her charming now. It all sounds as if it were made in heaven, but I have my doubts. Make the most of that, Aunt Jamesina.  <sub>[v3 c38 P16](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0016)</sub>
